stimulus:
A Fresnel lens is a strange thing: take a thick curved glass lens, slice it into concentric rings, throw away the bulky middle of each slice, and keep only the surface curvature. The bending of light survives the diet. Augustin Fresnel did this in the 1820s, and suddenly a lamp could be seen twenty miles out to sea. Before that, lighthouses used mirrors that lost most of the light to tarnish and soot.

The lens floats in a bath of mercury in many old towers, so a multi-ton assembly of brass and glass can spin with a nudge from a clockwork weight. Keepers wound that clockwork by hand, like feeding a very large cuckoo clock. Mercury, of course, is a nasty neighbor, and some keepers reportedly went strange, though that's a story I half remember rather than something I'd bet on.

The flash patterns are an alphabet: two seconds on, six off, identifies a particular rock. Each light has a signature, like a bird call or a Morse name. Daytime paint stripes do the same job, black spirals, red bands.

Then GPS arrived and the whole apparatus became charming rather than necessary. Yet theatre spotlights and car headlights borrowed the ridged trick, and so did the thin plastic magnifier sheets that sit in wallets. Overhead projectors too, those humming classroom machines with their warm glass tops and smudged transparencies.

Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Fresnel-style minimal-core reduction: which AP-1 features carry the memory?
ideas.description: Like a Fresnel lens keeps only the surface curvature that bends light, strip AP-1 down to its minimal functional elements by using domain-specific mutants of FOS/JUN (DNA-binding, dimerization, and pioneer-like or chromatin-remodeler recruitment domains). Then test which element is required for a stimulus-induced chromatin accessibility state to persist after the stimulus is removed, measured by ATAC-seq and H3K27ac CUT&Tag over several cell divisions.

ideas.title: Stimulus-withdrawal persistence time course with acute AP-1 degradation
ideas.description: Stimulate cells (e.g., with TPA, wounding signals, or inflammatory cues), then withdraw the stimulus. Use degron tags (dTAG/AID) to remove AP-1 factors at different times: during priming only, after washout only, or both. Track enhancer accessibility, AP-1 occupancy (CUT&RUN), and target gene re-inducibility to separate AP-1 as an initiator from AP-1 as a maintainer of the memory.

ideas.title: Lighthouse-signature dynamics: pulse-pattern encoding of memory
ideas.description: Lighthouses identify themselves by flash timing, so deliver identical total stimulus doses with different on/off patterns (e.g., 2 h on, 6 h off versus continuous). Do this using optogenetic or chemically inducible FOS/JUN, and read out with live-cell AP-1 reporters and single-cell RNA-seq or ATAC-seq. This tests whether AP-1 dynamics, not just level, determine whether a durable memory is written and how strongly secondary stimulation is primed.

ideas.title: Single-cell lineage-tracked memory inheritance
ideas.description: Mark cells with a live AP-1 reporter or endogenous tagged FOS/JUN and a heritable barcode. After transient stimulation, follow sister cells through division and test whether the AP-1 state and accessible chromatin are shared more between sisters than between random cells. Then compare the response of memory-positive and memory-negative sister lineages to restimulation, and use the results to model mitotic bookmarking and inheritance.

ideas.title: Targeted write/erase of AP-1 sites at specific enhancers
ideas.description: Use dCas9-based recruitment, or deletion/mutation of AP-1 motifs, at candidate memory enhancers (for example, those near genes with faster second responses). Test whether adding AP-1 sites is sufficient to create a primed, faster-responding state, and whether removing them abolishes it, without altering the global stimulus. Measure local accessibility, histone marks, nascent transcription (PRO-seq), and kinetics of the secondary response to establish site-specific causality.
